newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares firm early, tracking rise in Dow.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares firm early, tracking rise in Dow.

text.p: Singapore shares firmed in early trade on Wednesday garnering support from an overnight rally in Wall Street but institutional demand remained weak.
Dealers said that in the absence of local factors, the market was taking cues from overseas bourses.
"It's a mixed bag. Buying is coming in, helped by the Dow but it's a bit half-hearted," a local brokerage dealer said.
The Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) was up 4.91 points at 2,052.47 at 0230 GMT.
The UOB OTC index tracking mainly over the counter Malaysian shares, rebounded by 6.74 points to 1,183.61.
Selective buying of Singapore blue chip stocks continued, with dealers attributing demand to merely repositioning of investment portfolios and reallocation of assets.
Foreign tranches of banks drew buying interest early with UOB up Singapore 20 cents to S$14.80, DBS up 10 cents at S$17.70 and OCBC up 20 cents to S$17.80.
Foreign tranches of other stocks succumbed to profit-taking after strong rises previously. Among them were SPH, down 20 cents to S$27.30, and Singapore Airlines down 10 cents to S$12.
Singapore Telecom remained vulnerable, slipping to a new 1997 low of $2.60 in early trade.
